reasons: Classification is defensible: Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns binding provision that is silent on consent in either direction, so it fails the fallback's material requirement that assignments outside a successor transfer need consent (not unreasonably withheld) — particularly as to Vendor (HDI), which could otherwise transfer a hosting engagement holding our customer data to anyone, including a competitor.

No double-flagging or over-flagging: the rationale correctly records that there is no prohibition on Company assignment and no change-of-control trigger anywhere (so no walk-away exposure), and does not redline anything that benefits us.

Redline is valid and additive: the existing binding language is preserved verbatim and two sentences are appended granting the Company the affiliate/successor carve-out and imposing a reasonable-consent gate plus no-competitor limit on HDI — exactly the rule's redline guidance. The failed 'minimal edit' check is an artifact of the short source clause; the ratio reflects necessary additions, not a rewrite.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why in two sentences, and does not misdescribe the original clause.
Party naming ('Company', 'HDI') is consistent with the document; the added text does not conflict with the 'no other person shall acquire any rights' sentence.
